steps.what: Run the existing structure and browser checks
List checks that fail a stored standard
Evaluate whether the code is properly structured
Judge compatibility with browsers and devices
Sign the evaluation note
File the signed evaluation note
outputs: filed copy of signed evaluation note v1

tasks.design: The existing harness in {OPS_SYSTEM} already runs structure and browser checks. A job lists the checks that fail a stored standard. The developer evaluates the structure and judges compatibility with browsers, devices, or operating systems. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. The review is not shortened.
tasks.previous_blocker: Failed checks were copied out before the evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Check identifier and standard are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: A passing check can still be wrong for this site.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides whether the code meets the standard.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week evaluating, not on collecting failed checks.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.
Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests. Generated code is not treated as safe.

assumptions: Check identifier, standard, browser, and device are stored on the harness record. The harness record produces them. A blank standard stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the harness record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining evaluation time is still the developer evaluating the structure.

incremental.description: Refresh check identifier and standard when the harness layout changes, and drop a list the developer has not opened.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many standards are blank on the check. The high end assumes check identifier and standard are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored tables for the web application
Develop the database that supports the site
Review the schema before it is applied
Sign the database change
Apply only the signed database change
outputs: filed copy of signed database change v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored tables in {DATA_PLATFORM}. The developer develops the database and reviews the schema. A later job applies only that signed change. It cannot drop a database, and it does not run unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Table lists were copied before the schema was written.
tasks.enabler_now: Table identifier and column are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: A schema can still be the wrong model of the site.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the schema, not on listing tables.

reach.task: Apply only the signed database change

evidence.claim: Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests. Generated code is not treated as safe.
Digest [S28] says a coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions. This design makes no unattended live change.

assumptions: Table identifier, column, and application identifier are stored on the database record. The database record produces them. A blank column stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the database record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The apply job refuses any step that deletes a database. It applies only the signed set.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining development time is still the developer developing the database.

incremental.description: Refresh table identifier and column when the database layout changes, and drop a change the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the signed change is often sent back. The high end assumes table identifier and column are stored and the change applies once. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform tests on the planned schedule.

steps.what: Run tests already planned on the schedule
List tests due by interval or revision
Perform the due test after a revision
Judge the product result of that test
Sign the test note
File the signed test note
outputs: filed copy of signed test note v1

tasks.design: The harness in {OPS_SYSTEM} already runs tests on the planned schedule. A job lists tests due by the stored interval or by a later revision. The developer performs the due test and judges the product result. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. The harness runtime is not saved labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due tests were copied onto a sheet before the run.
tasks.enabler_now: The schedule interval, the last test, and the revision date are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The developer still judges the result.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides whether the product revision passed.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the due test, not on the scheduled harness.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.
The executive digest says scheduled link and accessibility checks already run.

assumptions: Test identifier, schedule interval, last test date, and revision date are stored on the test record. The test record produces them. A test is due when the interval has passed since the last test, or when the revision date is later than that last test. A blank interval is shown as not due, and a blank revision date does not by itself mark the row due.
Native configuration of the test record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining test time is still the developer performing the due test.

incremental.description: Refresh schedule interval, last test, and revision date when the harness layout changes, and drop a list the developer has not opened.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the interval or the revision date is blank. The high end assumes interval, last test, and revision date are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored pages in the update set
Direct which site updates are included
Perform the update on a branch first
Sign the site update set
Apply only the signed site update
outputs: filed copy of signed site update v1

tasks.design: A job lists the pages in {CMS}. The developer directs which updates are included and performs them on a branch. A later job applies only that signed set. It cannot drop a database, and it does not run unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Update pages were copied before the branch work.
tasks.enabler_now: Page identifier and revision are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The developer still has to make the update.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides which update goes out.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the update, not on listing pages.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests. Generated code is not treated as safe.
Digest [S28] says a coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions. This design makes no unattended live change.

assumptions: Page identifier, revision, and update action are stored on the content record. The content record produces them. A blank action stays blank and is not applied.
Native configuration of the content record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The apply job refuses any step that deletes a database. It applies only the signed set.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining direction time is still the developer directing the update.

incremental.description: Refresh page identifier and revision when the content layout changes, and drop an update the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the signed update is often sent back. The high end assumes page identifier and revision are stored and the update applies once. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The web developer spends the week writing, reviewing, and merging. A stored failing check, a blank field, and filing a signed note can move. The developer still reviews every change, and no job changes a live system alone.
reach: A reviewer reads the change before the developer merges it.
A specialist receives only the notice the developer signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a list that is missing a stored field.
Reject a sentence that does not restate a stored row.
Reject a live change that is not the signed set.
role.ambitious_version: A signed change can be filed the same week, and the developer still owns the merge.
